questions.prompt: What is the plasma frequency of a three-dimensional electron gas of density $n$ and effective mass $m$?
questions.solution: The plasma frequency is $\omega_p=\sqrt{ne^2/(m\epsilon_0)}$ (Eq. 14.77). The first option is $\omega_p^2$, not $\omega_p$. The second has no mass. The third is a product of a velocity and a wave number.

questions.prompt: At high density, why are the bubble-chain diagrams the leading terms in the self-energy?
questions.solution: At high density ($r_s\to0$) the low-order diagrams dominate, because the scaling of each diagram with $k_F$, equivalently $r_s$, makes a diagram of order $n$ larger than one of higher order $n'>n$ (Eqs. 14.6-14.7). Within a given order the most divergent diagram dominates: the divergence number $\delta$ counts the interaction lines that carry the same small momentum, and the diagram with $\delta=n$ diverges most strongly as $q\to0$ (Eqs. 14.8-14.9). That diagram at each order is a chain of pair bubbles (Eq. 14.10). Summing these chains is the RPA resummation of Eqs. (14.11)-(14.14).

questions.prompt: Write the RPA interaction as a series in the bare interaction $W$ and the pair bubble $\chi_0$. Give its static long-wavelength form with the Thomas-Fermi wavenumber $k_s$.
Landau damping of a plasmon occurs when:
choices: the plasmon dispersion enters the particle-hole continuum, where $\mathrm{Im}\,\chi^R_0\neq0$
questions.solution: A pole of Eq. (14.79) lies on the real axis only where $\mathrm{Im}\,\chi^R_0=0$. Where the plasmon enters the particle-hole continuum, the pole broadens into a Lorentzian and the mode is damped (Eqs. 14.79-14.80; Eq. 14.30 for the continuum). The conditions in the other options are not the criterion.

questions.prompt: Book Exercise 14.1. Classical derivation of $\omega_p$. Displace a slab of electrons of density $n$ by a distance $\xi$ perpendicular to its surfaces, against the uniform positive background. Find the restoring field and the frequency of the oscillation.
questions.solution:
The displacement leaves a surface charge $\pm ne\xi$ on the two faces of the slab. Each face contributes $ne\xi/(2\epsilon_0)$ to the field, so the field inside is $E=ne\xi/\epsilon_0$. Each electron feels a force $-eE$, so
$$m\ddot\xi=-\frac{ne^2}{\epsilon_0}\,\xi\quad\Rightarrow\quad \omega_p=\sqrt{\frac{ne^2}{m\epsilon_0}}.$$
No $\hbar$ appears, which is the classical result of Eq. (14.77).

questions.prompt: Book Exercise 14.2. A two-dimensional electron gas in GaAs ($m^*=0.067m$, $\varepsilon_r=13$). Show that the two-dimensional Fourier transform of the Coulomb interaction $\frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0 r}$ is $W^{2D}(q)=\dfrac{e^2}{2\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0 q}$.
questions.solution:
Use $\int d^2r\,e^{-i\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf r}f(r)=2\pi\int_0^\infty dr\,r\,f(r)J_0(qr)$. For $f=e^2/(4\pi\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0r)$,
$$W^{2D}(q)=\frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0}\,2\pi\int_0^\infty dr\,J_0(qr)=\frac{e^2}{2\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0}\cdot\frac1q=\frac{e^2}{2\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0\,q},$$
using $\int_0^\infty J_0(qr)\,dr=1/q$ (the hint $\int_0^\pi d\theta\cos(\alpha\cos\theta)=\pi J_0(\alpha)$ gives the angular integral).

questions.prompt: Book Exercise 14.3 (homework). For a two-dimensional gas use $\varepsilon_{\rm RPA}=1-W^{2D}(q)\chi^{2D}_0(q,\omega)$ with the high-frequency limit $\chi^{2D}_0\approx n_{2D}q^2/(m^*\omega^2)$. Find the plasmon dispersion and show that it is gapless, with $k_F=\sqrt{2\pi n_{2D}}$.
questions.solution:
Setting $\varepsilon_{\rm RPA}=0$ gives $1=W^{2D}(q)\,n_{2D}q^2/(m^*\omega^2)$. Inserting $W^{2D}(q)=e^2/(2\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0q)$,
$$\omega^2(q)=\frac{n_{2D}e^2}{2\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0m^*}\,q\quad\Rightarrow\quad \omega(q)=\sqrt{\frac{n_{2D}e^2\,q}{2\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0m^*}}\propto\sqrt q.$$
The mode has no gap at $q=0$, unlike the three-dimensional plasmon of Eq. (14.78). The Fermi wavenumber follows from $n_{2D}=2\cdot\pi k_F^2/(2\pi)^2=k_F^2/(2\pi)$, so $k_F=\sqrt{2\pi n_{2D}}$.

questions.prompt: Book Exercise 14.4. For the two-dimensional gas take the static pair bubble at small $q$ as $\chi^{2D}_0(q\to0,0)=-m^*/(\pi\hbar^2)$ (both spins). Show that $W^{2D}_{\rm RPA}(q,0)=\dfrac{e^2}{2\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0\,(q+k_s^{2D})}$ with $k_s^{2D}=2/a_0^*$ and $a_0^*=4\pi\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0\hbar^2/(m^*e^2)$.
questions.solution:
From Eq. (14.16) with $W^{2D}=e^2/(2\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0q)$,
$$W^{2D}_{\rm RPA}=\frac{W^{2D}}{1-W^{2D}\chi_0^{2D}}=\frac{W^{2D}}{1+W^{2D}d^{2D}},\qquad d^{2D}=\frac{m^*}{\pi\hbar^2}.$$
Multiplying numerator and denominator by $2\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0q$ gives $e^2/[2\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0(q+k_s^{2D})]$ with
$$k_s^{2D}=\frac{e^2d^{2D}}{2\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0}=\frac{e^2m^*}{2\pi\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0\hbar^2}=\frac{2}{a_0^*}.$$
The last step uses $a_0^*=4\pi\varepsilon_r\epsilon_0\hbar^2/(m^*e^2)$.
